catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class runs one closed-loop policy control step: the motion classes command joint or Cartesian targets, velocities or torques, while this action advances the upstream BipedController.step() and returns the motor target and policy action it computed. The package uses this extension with an inline output schema.

cap.motion.stop.v1 asks for a deceleration profile and reports a stopping position; BipedController.shutdown() takes no deceleration and reports no position, so the safe-state action is an extension with an inline boolean output. It is the achieved_by action of the declared safe state and is also the e-stop path.

Passed on the fake backend (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). No hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed. The final gate run raised no warning on any gate. This package is model-authored (authored_by kind model, deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run wD-013) and reviewed_by is null: the loader refuses its R2 hardware backend until a human signs it. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names the PythonObjectDriver helper; this package uses a direct Driver because the reads are fields of nested upstream objects (BipedController.sensor_data and MotorController.dof_pos/dof_vel/dof_current) that the config-only family cannot bind as read paths. Covered: the 10 joint positions, velocities and currents, the motor target, the four raw load-cell values, the two foot-contact flags, the filtered angular velocity, the gravity vector, the base quaternion, the sensor sample rate and the three upstream command values; the three command writes (cap.device.configure.v1) are Limit.operator_required because the clone states no command envelope (the gamepad scaling at gamepad.py:6-8 is teleop, not a device bound); x-cap.generalroboticslab.step.v1 runs one BipedController.step(); x-cap.generalroboticslab.stop.v1 is the safe-state action, and the e-stop calls the same BipedController.shutdown(). Not covered: the learned policy checkpoint and its observation/action scaling, the EtherCAT transport itself, the Teensy firmware, the physical e-stop (the clone documents none), joint-space position or torque commands, and linear acceleration (the clone states no unit for the filtered value). The fake returns full-size arrays (10 joints, 4 load cells, 3-vector, 4-quaternion, 2 contacts). The upstream step() also runs check_termination(), which calls exit() when the controller decides to reset (biped_controller.py:240-247); that is upstream behaviour and the fake does not exercise it. native.py is the deployment-only factory; the gate never imports it or the clone. site-limits.example.json repeats the gamepad teleop scaling only as an example operator choice, not a device bound. The upstream environment is Python 3.8 (setup/conda_env.yaml:11), and deploying it needs the build/ethercat_motor_py extension (README.md:105-120), motor_config.yaml (motor_controller.py:67-70) and checkpoint/baseline (biped_controller.py:34-44).

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-30; reviewed_by stays null): accepted after reviewer edits. The e-stop, the safe-state action and the teardown called BipedController.shutdown(), which sets the motor loop's terminate flag and then never returns: SerialDataCollector.stop() clears a flag in the calling process and joins its multiprocessing child without a timeout, and the child never sees the flag (sensor_controller.py:6, 129-140). They now make the motor part of the upstream's own termination (check_termination, biped_controller.py:244-245): every motor's torque limit to 0, which the motor loop writes to the drives every cycle (src/ethercat_motor.h:361-364, 957), then the terminate flag; they also set the three command values to 0, the native event gate G6 sees (it does not see calls on the nested motor object). The fake's shutdown, which cleared the command values although the upstream's does not, is gone, and its motor records the two setters. For the human reviewer: the stop leaves the biped without joint torque, so it falls unless it is supported; a termination inside step() (a tilt above 45 degrees or a reset flag) waits in the same shutdown(), so that step action does not return; and BipedController takes cmd arrays and a reset flag from any sender on UDP port 9871 (biped_controller.py:173-175, 315-322). driver.py, fake.py, test_driver.py, facts.md and the reference changed; the author's files are kept in work/handoff-runs/wD/reviewer-originals/. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required: the licence is not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published before it. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
